evidence: Iron Fist S1 episode 8: Ward and Joy are voted out of Rand Enterprises by Lawrence Wilkins and the shareholders (given severance). Episode 13: after Harold's death Ward proposes he and Danny run the company together and becomes co-CEO again. The firing and the return are both unrecorded.

Daredevil S2 episode 9: Foggy tells Matt that Nelson and Murdock should shut down and Matt agrees; the firm ends. In The Defenders Matt works pro bono on his own while Foggy is at Hogarth, Chao & Benowitz. So the group ends in Daredevil S2, which no stage or left records.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day shows MJ at MIT with Ned (her major changes to aerospace). She graduates in 2028, moves back to New York with Ned, and is job-hunting (she skips an interview). She no longer works at the donut shop. The wiki infobox still lists Peter Pan Donut with no 'formerly', so this is medium.

X-Men '97 S1E3 (episode 3): with her powers gone for good, 'a shell-shocked Storm decided to leave the team' and wanders to Texas, where she meets Forge. In S1E6 she regains her powers and returns as the team learns of the attack on Genosha; she leads the Gold Team in episode 10. Neither her quitting nor her return is recorded.

Inhumans episode 4: Black Bolt and Medusa capture Locus after an explosion knocks her out. Episode 5: they keep her in Louise's car trunk as a prisoner and use her power to find Karnak. She tells them she still believes in Maximus's promise. She is shot in the fight with Tua's traffickers. Being captured is custody, not leaving the group, and she never defects. Her dying words to Black Bolt, asking him to change Attilan and telling him Crystal is on Oahu, do not put her in another group. MCU Wiki lists Black Bolt and Medusa as her 'Kidnapper'.

Flint Marko was a U.S. soldier in World War I and was captured and experimented on in France (Spider-Noir S1E5). After the war he went to work for Silvermane (S1E4) and stayed with him until Cat killed Silvermane (S1E8). The record puts the Army after the mob, which says he left Silvermane to rejoin the Army. He never does. The Army comes first in the story. The Independent stage and the left entry stand: Silvermane's death ends the mob, and Flint and Cat start a new life.

MCU Wiki, section 'Nick Fury's Crew': in 2018 Hill left Stark Industries and joined Nick Fury (cited to the Captain Marvel Prelude comic and the Secret Invasion production brief). On screen she is first seen working at Fury's side in Avengers: Infinity War, where she turns to dust next to him. She is still with him in Secret Invasion episode 1. The infobox lists Nick Fury's Crew among her affiliations.

Elena walks out of S.H.I.E.L.D. and the Secret Warriors in S3 episode 17 ('The Team', episode 61 overall), then comes back to S.H.I.E.L.D. at the Playground and fights Hive by S3 episode 20 (episode 64). So her return to S.H.I.E.L.D. happens in Season 3, not in Slingshot. Slingshot only shows her signing the Accords with an agency she had already rejoined.

WandaVision episodes 5-6: after Wanda's confrontation, Hayward has Darcy, Jimmy Woo and Monica Rambeau ordered off the S.W.O.R.D. Response Base and escorted out (removed from the operation); they overpower the escort, break back in, and Darcy hacks Hayward's files and turns against him. She is never back with S.W.O.R.D. (Thor: Love and Thunder has her with Jane only). The MCU wiki lists no S.W.O.R.D. affiliation for her.

Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S7, episode 13 (the series finale, 'What We're Fighting For'): with the Chronicom invasion over, Fitz and Simmons retire from S.H.I.E.L.D. to raise Alya; a year later Daisy calls him 'retired' at the virtual reunion. Retirement is a departure under the rules, and the record's last stage is still S.H.I.E.L.D. with no left entry.

Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S7, episode 13 (the series finale, 'What We're Fighting For'): with the Chronicom invasion over, Fitz and Simmons retire from S.H.I.E.L.D. to raise Alya; a year later Daisy calls him 'retired' at the virtual reunion. Retirement is a departure under the rules, and the record's last stage is still S.H.I.E.L.D. with no left entry. (Same person as A:st-leo-fitz; this file's last stage is also S.H.I.E.L.D.)

Daredevil: Born Again S2, episode 3: Daredevil frees the Task Force's detainees at Red Hook, Soledad among them. They are taken to Ariana's safehouse, where the fugitives record testimony against Fisk for Daredevil and Karen (episode 4). The MCU Wiki lists Soledad as a member of Daredevil's Army (the resistance) and gives that as her affiliation.

Bakuto's time in K'un-Lun is backstory: he trained there centuries ago, was banished with Alexandra, Gao, Sowande and Murakami, and they founded the Hand (revealed in The Defenders ep 4). In The Defenders he is with the Hand the whole time. He never leaves the Hand for K'un-Lun, so a K'un-Lun stage after his Iron Fist S1 Hand stage is wrong.

In season 2 (from the episode 'Afterlife', ep 38), after her Terrigenesis, Raina is taken to Afterlife, the Inhuman settlement. With Gordon's help she accepts her place there ('embrace my life here... to help my people') and stays until Jiaying kills her (ep 43). The app already uses the group 'Afterlife' for Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S2, as in Lincoln Campbell's record. Her season 2 work for Whitehall was forced on her with a control device, so it is not a move.

At the end of Across the Spider-Verse, Peter B. goes against Miguel and the Spider-Society and joins Gwen's band to bring Miles home. That is turning on the group. Marvel Database lists Spider Society as a former affiliation and gives Spider-Gang as his current one. Gwen Stacy's record already leaves the Society in this film the same way (Spider-Society, then Independent).

Marvel Database files the 1967 animated series' Charles Cameo as Earth-6799 (first appearance: Spider-Man (1967 animated series) Season 1 10B). Its Earth-67 is a comics-only offshoot from Spider-Verse Team-Up, described as 'a divergent version of Earth-6799'. Note: the app uses Earth-67 for about 33 records of this series, so the same fix applies to all of them.

Marvel Database files the Master Technician of the 1967 animated series as Earth-6799 (Reality = Earth-6799, first appearance Season 2 3). Earth-6799 is the reality of the 1967 cartoon. Earth-67 is a comics-only offshoot of it.

What If...? S1 episode 9: after the Guardians of the Multiverse are sent home, the Watcher places Natasha in the universe that lost its Widow (Earth-51825); she stops Loki on the Helicarrier and Nick Fury offers her a place in that world's new Avengers. Both wikis list her current affiliation as the Avengers of that world and the Guardians as former.

X-Men '97 S2 episode 2 (episode 12 overall): X-Force tracks Emma down and she leads them into a trap set by X-Factor. She is not an X-Factor member. Marvel Database's X-Factor (Earth-92131) roster leaves her out and files this under her 'Solo career', with Genosha as a former base and the Interim Council as a former affiliation. Wikipedia names X-Factor as Cooper's team of Havok, Polaris, Multiple Man, Strong Guy and Wolfsbane. Genosha was destroyed in S1, so by S2 she belongs to no group.

In the altered 1983 (on file at episode 135), S.H.I.E.L.D. trainee Garrett joins Nathaniel Malick's crew in S7 'Stolen' (episode 133). In S7 'The End is at Hand' (episode 135), after Malick leaves him to die in the Lighthouse, he turns his back on Malick and rejoins S.H.I.E.L.D. He teleports Coulson, May and Yo-Yo out, and Victoria Hand then shoots him. The record ends on HYDRA from S1, with no S7 stages.

X-Men '97 S1 episode 9 ('Tolerance Is Extinction, Part 2'): Forge and Storm answer Xavier's call and rejoin the X-Men, rescue Jubilee and Roberto, and Forge is put on Gold Team against Bastion; in S1 episode 10 he is already running the X-Men's roster at the mansion. He joins in S1, not S2.

Eyes of Wakanda episode 4: Prince Tafari is on his first War Dogs (Hatut Zaraze) mission with Kuda, returns the axe to Adwa and reports back to Wakanda with Kuda. He never leaves the War Dogs on screen. Both wikis list him as a War Dogs member now. So the closing 'Wakanda' stage (which reads as him leaving the War Dogs) has no move behind it.

proposed: Split the record. Keep the episode 98 step (the original Flint, who stays in 2091) here as Earth-17516. Move the episode 122 and season 7 steps to a new record for the duplicate Flint that Mack and Yo-Yo create with the Di'Allas in the present day, earth null (Earth-199999), group Independent.
evidence: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S5 episode 10: the original Flint stays in the 2091 future (Earth-17516) to rebuild Earth. S6 episode 11 onward: a new Flint is made from Mack and Elena's memories with the Di'Allas of Creation in 2019 (Earth-199999). That one appears in S6 and S7. Marvel Database files them as two characters in two realities.

In What If...? episode 2 Carina starts as the Collector's slave/assistant in his museum (Tivan Group). She turns on him by shooting Ebony Maw, freeing T'Challa, and using the Collector's bracelet to free his captives. Both wikis list the Tivan Group as a former affiliation, and she joins no other group.

Laura retired from S.H.I.E.L.D. (as Agent 19) before any title she is on file for. Fury hid her from the files and set up the farm, all before Avengers: Age of Ultron. Hawkeye only reveals that past through her watch; nothing there puts her back in S.H.I.E.L.D. So the S.H.I.E.L.D./Hawkeye stage is wrong, and neither Age of Ultron nor Hawkeye shows a departure on screen, so both left titles fail G3 too. (If the owner wants the past recorded, the alternative is S.H.I.E.L.D. from the start, then Independent with no left.)

What If...? episode 17 (S2E8, 'What If... The Avengers Assembled in 1602?'): Wanda is the court merlin/advisor to the Asgardian royal family (King Thor's court) and is one of the band of heroes (with Hela, Thor and Fury) who summon Captain Carter; when the band fights King Thor she betrays her king, restrains him, and helps Carter find the Forerunner. Marvel Database lists her affiliation as the Avengers (Earth-TRN1093); the app already files Tony (1602) under The Avengers and King Thor under Asgard.

The Punisher S2 (episode 6 onward): Anderson and Eliza Schultz founded and run Testament Industries, the company behind their wealth and their son's career. The owner's rule says companies count as groups, and both of them belong to it in every title they're on file for.

Murakami's time in K'un-Lun is centuries-old backstory: he and the other four founders perverted K'un-Lun's teachings and were banished, forming the Hand. Throughout The Defenders he is one of the Hand's five leaders (fighting the Defenders, caught in the Midland Circle collapse); he is never in K'un-Lun from that title, so the K'un-Lun stage (and the duplicated Hand stage) is wrong.

Enoch is a Chronicom anthropologist, not a S.H.I.E.L.D. member, when he first appears (episode 88, S4E22, he freezes and abducts Coulson's team) and through S5-S6 he acts on his own mission (in S6 he leaves FitzSimmons to find a home for his people, then goes undercover among the Chronicom Hunters). In episode 123 (S6E13 'New Life') he turns on the hunters to save Fitz and Simmons and devises the plan with them; from S7 he serves with the team on Zephyr One.

The third stage moves Cornell from the Stokes Crime Family back to Harlem's Paradise, but nothing in Luke Cage S1 moves him: he leads the Stokes Crime Family and owns Harlem's Paradise right up until Mariah kills him in episode 7. The wiki lists both affiliations as current. The duplicate last stage has no on-screen move behind it.

At the end of X-Men: Apocalypse the Horsemen are finished: Angel dies, Magneto and Storm turn on Apocalypse, and he is destroyed. Psylocke then walks away from the X-Men. The X-Men Movies wiki lists the Horsemen of Apocalypse as a former affiliation. The group ending is a move under the rules.
